newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia Q1 handset margin hit 10 pct - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Nokia Q1 handset margin hit 10 pct - CEO.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy's chief executive Jorma Ollila said on Tuesday that Nokia had reached its target 10 percent margin in mobile phone sales in the first quarter.
"We did reach that level during the first quarter," Ollila told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
"The mobile phones were able to come out of the logistical problems that we had in the first half of last year particularly well," he said.
Releasing Q1 earnings earlier, Nokia said mobile phone sales rose 58 percent year-on-year and that the division's operating profit had improved "signifiantly" on the year-ago period.
Handset price erosion had continued, but Ollila said Nokia had "more than matched" it thanks to increased productivity and "very good volume growth".
"We expect this year an average (handset price) erosion of 15-20 percent, which we can very well manage," he said.
Ollila said Nokia had "very well kept our market share" in mobile phones, "and in fact strengthened that in many parts of the world". He did not elaborate.
He said the market growth had been around 50 percent in value terms, and growth "is almost going to continue at that level during the next 18 months, pretty much at the same level."
"Since we are a clear leader in the digital handsets it is only feasible to expect that we will continue to maintain our good share in the very tough competitive mobile phone market," Ollila said.
More efficient supply chain management and delivery of products through the pipeline were key objectives, he said.
Looking back at the first quarter, Ollila said Nokia had achieved "strong growth" in both its core businesses.

The infrastructure division, telecommunications, had 34 percent sales growth, and Ollila said its profitability had remained "on a very good level". Nokia does not release quarterly profit figures by business group.

Consolidated Q1 profit before tax and minority interest surged over 260 percent to 1.45 billion markka. Group net sales rose to 11.33 billion markka from 7.93 billion. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
